tei:div.tei:ab: 7. Dynamik u. Vortrag, metodisch als Einheit u. Ausdruck der Synthese; wiederholt Gesd-Etude u. Brahms-Walzer No 2.

10. Trägt in mein Urlinieblatt des Jhrb. die Urlinie-studie ein,That is, the foreground graphs to the essays on Chopin’s etudes Op. 10, Nos. 5 and 6, published in the first volume of Das Meisterwerk in der Musik. ich korrigire Schichten u. dynamische Zeichen in dem Bild. Plötzlich meinte B.: er möchte die Préludes spielen „. . nur so, nur zu wissen wie man sie übt“Diary Oct 10, 1929: “Brünauer pays half, at the end of the lesson in which we have made such an interesting study for the first time [to discover] the methodical foundations of Chopin's dynamic markings; he says he would like to ask me: ‘Show me how one should practice the Preludes.’ I decline.” – Ich lehne streng ab u. rufe ihn zur Ordnung. Chopin: No 7, Cdur.

14. Etude Cdur No 7 neu; ich skizzire die Linie u. erkläre sie, lehre ihn, wie diese Etude geübt werden soll: zuerst die Finger 2 1, die Spannungen der Quint u. Sext, der Sinn der legato-Wirkung usw. wiederholt Stellen aus Schubert Me-
-nuett Hm.
21. Wiederholt u. arbeitet metodisch durch Nocturne Fisdur bis doppio movimento, jede Bewegung festgelegt.
24. Etude Fdur op. 10VIII neu, bis zum mittleren Teil.

28. Entrüstet sich über die offenbar in einer Gesellschaft gehörte Wendung von „Bruckner-Thränen“ in bezug auf die VIII. Sinf.A long entry in Schenker’s diary for October 28, 1929 begins: “Brünauer is very agitated and upset for being reproached for the tears wept on the occasion of hearing Bruckner's Eighth Symphony! Now since he is so constituted as to never reveal his emotions about similar things […] it merely remains for me to content myself with the suspicion that somewhere he was reproached for shedding tears as a sign of Bruckner's greatness, but that he was not in the position to rebut this foolish argument, so that in the end he suffered a setback. But since his excitement at the same time contained an appeal to my authority, which was supposed to decide about the worth or worthlessness of Bruckner, I could not now deny myself giving him a definition of Bruckner that would be useful to him and ease his burden […]” Bekennt sich zur Heimwehr! Nascht die Polonaise Cism Mittelteil.
4. XI. Nascht aus Händels Suite Edur den Vortrag des Variationen Themas.
11. Das Bild der Etude Fd sehr sauber eingetragen, fast die Grenze des für ihn Erreichbaren. Spielt den 1. Teil nun fast ganz gut.

14. Aus Anlaß von Händel u. non legato über Liebhaber als meine Schüler, ich verfolge dieses Thema geschichtlich bis zu Brahms u. Bach, deren
Schüler ebenfalls Liebhaber waren.

18. Zeige Beispiele von Schönberg in einem seiner letzten Aufsätze zu Bachs 1. Cism-Präludium u. aus Mozarts Dissonanten-Quartett.Arnold Schoenberg, Zur Frage des modernen Kompositionsunterrichtes, Deutsche Tonkünstlerzeitung, (November 5, 1929); Eng. transl. Leo Black, On the Question of Modern Composition Teaching, in Style and Idea, ed. Leonard Stein (London: Faber & Faber, 1975), pp. 374–75.
25. Aus Anlaß der „Meistersinger“ über Wagner: eine Urlinie fehlt! Zeige Bilder der Eroica, Scherzo 1. Teil, Trauermarsch u. Rückleitung.

2. XII. Ueber Casals Konzert;The concert took place in the large hall of the Konzerthaus on Saturday November 30, with Pablo Casals, cello, and Otto Schulhof, piano. The program included Bach’s solo Suite in E and Beethoven’s Cello Sonata Op. 102, No. 2. Schuberts Menuett begonnen.
5. Chopin op. 25I begonnen; er liest den II. Bd. des Kontrapunkts, wie er sagt.
9. Ueber Beethovens Missa; Schubert Menuett wiederholt.
12. Bringt ein selbst verfaßtes Bild der Asdur Etude, auch ein Bild zur Coda der Fd Etude; ich trage Fingersatz ein.

16. Ueber das Philharmonische Konzert:Schenker heard the Vienna Philharmonic Orchestra on December 14, 1929, and recorded a long entry in his diary for that day, which begins: “At 3 o'clock, on foot to the Philharmonic concert: Haydn, Symphony in G major, the so-called "Military", Respighi Roman Festivals, and Schumann's Symphony No. 1 in B major. Haydn was a failure!! Respighi enjoyed a great reception, in spite of not rising above the barbarisms of the Italian side-streets. [...]” Haydns sog. Militär-Sinfonie; Respighi usw.

23. Vierhändig gespielt: Haydn Gdur-Sinfonie Adagio 6/8.Possibly the Symphony in G, Hob. I:81, the slow movement of which is an Andante (not Adagio) in 6/8. None of Haydn’s later G major symphonies has a slow movement in 6/8 meter.

30. Bringt eige-
-ne Walzer, ich improvisire Korrekturen.
2. I. Noch einmal die Walzer, ich vertage die Korrektur auf den 15.

9. Präludium von S. Bach aus dem Wohltemp. Klavier nach Linie, Metrik u. Dynamik aus Anlaß von v. Cubes Anfrage.In OJ 9/34, [20], January 2, 1930, Cube to Schenker: “For the Deutsche Tonkünstler-Zeitung I am working on an article Urlinie and Piano Teaching or A Lesson with Bach, and for this purpose I have chosen the first C major prelude from the Well-Tempered Clavier. I hope I have read it correctly.” – There follows an extended analysis of the Urlinie of the Prelude.
16. Holt zu einem politischen Gespräch aus über die Schwierigkeiten in Deutschland u. Oesterreich.
20. Ueber Romain Rolland aus Anlaß meiner Anfrage Anführung; Brahms Walzer Asd genau.
23. Das Bild der Coda aus der Etude Fd, gründlich noch einmal; Vortrag der Etude 25I, methodisch.

27. Ueber das Konzert Backhaus:According to the website of the piano manufacturers Bechstein (Bechstein/Backhaus), Wilhelm Backhaus performed the complete cycle of Beethoven’s 32 piano sonatas in Vienna and Paris in December 1929. ich zeige die Cism-Sonate, 1. u. 2. Satz, trage auch den Vortrag ein, arbeite ihn methodisch durch erkläre sogar die Urlinie.
30. Letzter Satz der Cism-Sonate flüchtig; das Bild von op. 25I neu gemacht, ich korrigire es.

tei:div.tei:ab: October 3: Etude in E minor, new; fingering.
October 7: Dynamics and performance, methodically as a unity and an expression of the synthesis; Etude in G major revisited, and Brahms’s Waltz No. 2.

October 10: He enters his Urlinie study into my Urlinie graph in the Yearbook; I correct the structural levels and dynamic markings in the graph. Suddenly Brünauer says that he would like to play the preludes “only in such a way as to know how one should practise them – I decline in the strictest terms and call him to order. Chopin: No. 7 in C major.

October 14:Etude No. 7 in C major, new; I sketch the voice-leading line and explain it, teaching him how this etude is to be practiced: to begin with, the fingering 2 1, the tensions in the intervals of a fifth and a sixth, the meaning of the legato effect, etc. He repeats passages from Schubert’s
Minuet in B minor.
October 21: He revisits and works methodically through the Nocturne in F major as far as the doppio movimento, every motion clearly determined.
October 24: Etude in F major, Op. 10, No. 8, new, as far as the middle section.

October 28: He is indignant about the expression “Bruckner tears,” evidently heard at a party, concerning the Eighth Symphony. Confesses to belonging to the Home Guard! Nibbles at the middle section of the Polonaise in C minor.
October 31: Etude in F major, up to the coda.
November 4: He nibbles at the performance of the variation theme from Handel’s Suite in E major.
November 11: The graph of the Etude in F major, entered very cleanly, nearly at the limit of what he is capable of. He now plays the first part very well almost throughout.

November 14: With reference to Handel and non legato, with concern for the amateurs who are my pupils, I follow this subject historically as far as Brahms and Bach, whose
pupils were likewise amateurs.
November 18: I show him examples from Schoenberg in one of his recent essays, on Bach’s first C minor Prelude and Mozart’s “Dissonance” Quartet.

November 25: With reference to Die Meistersinger, concerning Wagner: an Urlinie is absent! I show him graphs of the “Eroica”: the first part of the Scherzo, and the Funeral March and its retransition.
December 5: Chopin’s Op. 25, No. 1, begun; he is reading the second volume of my Counterpoint, so he says.
December 9: Concerning Beethoven’s Missa solemnis; Schubert’s Minuet revisited.
December 12:He brings a graph of the A major Etude that he made himself, also a graph of the coda of the F major Etude; I enter fingering.
December 16: Concerning the Philharmonic concert: Haydn’s so-called “Military” Symphony; Respighi, etc.
December 19: Performance of the Etude in A major.
December 23: The Adagio in 6/8 from Haydn’s Symphony in G major, played four-hands.

December 30: He brings
waltzes of his own composition; I improvise corrections.
January 2: Once again, the waltzes; I delay making corrections until the 15th.
January 9: J. S. Bach’s Prelude from the Well-Tempered Clavier, with respect to voice-leading line, metric organization, and dynamics, in connection with Cube’s question.
January 16: He launches into a political discussion about the difficulties in Germany and Austria.
January 20: On Romain Rolland in connection with my mentioning him; Brahms’s Waltz in A major played precisely.
January 23: The graph of the coda of the Etude in F major, once again thoroughly; performance of the Etude Op. 25, No. 1, methodical.
January 27: On Backhaus’s concert: I show him the C minor Sonata, first and second movement; I also enter the performance marks, working through them methodically, and even explain the Urlinie.
January 30: Last movement of the C minor Sonata, hastily. The graph of Op. 25, No. 1, remade; I correct it.
